rulings: Byte count: the screen shows `1679022 bytes`, the raw source string. Thousands separators are a restatement, so they are not used. Ruled by the Studio Lead 2026-10-19 after the storyboard critic flagged it.
F3 cites claude-run.js:630 in its source sentence and :631 in its verification. No line number appears on screen or in the copy; only the file name and the line's text, which were both read this run.

The frames inside the tile are the piece's own abstraction. F4 verifies that a 1679022-byte video/mp4 attachment existed, nothing about its contents, so the tile may never imitate the real video's pixels. Disclosed on the page, in post.txt and in alt.txt.

The revival may not be edited as the result of the fix. Amended 2026-10-19: the commit and its tests are now read and verified (F5, F6), but its deployment is not, and unverified items 3 and 4 still allow for other causes. So the piece places three verified stamps in their verified order — 08:53:00.940 dead, 09:17:23 the line rewritten, 11:55:54.668 the file — with no arrow, join or wipe between them, and both conditions stay lit under the second render. The order is shown; the cause is not claimed.

The film's single editorial line, `it was killed to ask nothing.`, is our wording, traced to F3 (`questions: []`, an empty question treated as a real one) and F1 (the run was ended, nothing was delivered). Declared editorial, not quoted as a source sentence.
The render's own duration is not verified, so no render length, frame count or percentage appears anywhere. The interactive dial's scale is a model and is labelled as one.

The clock never animates between the two verified timestamps: interpolating them would draw dozens of millisecond-precision UTC values that never existed. It cuts on the beat instead. Ruled 2026-10-19 after the second critic found 10:54:27.804 on screen.
No invented number is drawn inside the picture. The interactive dial's value is HTML chrome, a control the reader is moving, and the only timeout printed on the canvas is the measured 120 s.

The dial has exactly one evidenced position and it is 120 s. Re-ruled 2026-10-19 after QA found that any value below the render length wore `08:53:00.940 UTC` and `0 attachments` while the page said "the run we actually have" — 250 s was being dressed as evidence. The rule is now a single test, `dialSec === 120`, not a branch: at 120 the card wears the verified timestamp and the `0 attachments` chip and the page may call it the evidenced run; at every other value, on either side of the render, the header reads `model run`, there is no timestamp, there is no attachment row, and the page says this one was not measured. The dial snaps to 120 so the reader can always get back to the evidence. 11:55:54.668, video_post_en.mp4, 1679022 bytes and 3 h 2 min appear only in the film.
'3 hours' is never written anywhere, including UI copy: the replay button says 'Replay the 3 h 2 min'.
'an object, so truthy' in post.txt and the word 'truthy' on screen describe JavaScript's own semantics, not the incident, so they are not a second editorial claim about what happened.

The dial's render bar is drawn longer than the 120 s mark, which is the mechanism's premise (the render outlived the call). No duration is printed, and the page says in words that the handle is a model and only the orange mark is a measured value. Ruling 6 still holds: no render length is stated anywhere.

The code in the fix panel comes from `git show 60f0e18 -- lib/claude-run.js`. Exactly three things are done to it, all of them formatting: leading indentation is trimmed; long lines are wrapped (the removed line is drawn on two rows, as the mechanism has always drawn it); and braces are re-placed where a wrap forces it, so `if (asked) {` + `question = asked;` is drawn as `if (asked) { question = asked; }` and `} else if (...) {` loses its leading brace. The added block is also a subset: `opts.onQuestion`, `endOnQuestion` and `unreadableQuestionId` are not drawn. No token is renamed, paraphrased or invented, nothing is drawn that is not in the commit, and no line numbers appear (ruling 2 still holds). Note the deliberate inconsistency with the mechanism, which has always drawn `questions: [ ]` with a space to make the emptiness visible; the diff panel is character-exact at `questions: []`.

The test pass is shown as the counts the run actually printed — `tests 29`, `pass 29`, `fail 0` — beside the file that produced them, never as an animated ticking green check or a progress bar filling. One named test is quoted exactly from the run's output so a reader can grep for it. Ruled 2026-10-19 when F6 was added.

Numbers added with F5 and F6 join the copy rule: `09:17:23 UTC`, `60f0e18`, `29`, `0`. `60f0e18` is the short hash the repository's own log prints; the full hash is in F5's source. Never "a few tests", "all tests" or "the build is green".

The fix panel is on screen while the card behind it still reads `08:53:00.940 UTC` and `0 attachments`, at about a tenth of its brightness. Checked against the no-false-pairing rule and allowed: the card is an immutable record of a message that was posted, not a live clock, and it was still that message, still with no attachment, at 09:17:23. The pairing the rule exists to stop is the opposite case — `0 attachments` beside `11:55:54.668 UTC`, which would say the delivery arrived empty — and that one is still prevented by retiring the chip 24 frames before the clock cuts.
